metadata.title: Altitude-Resolved Spatial Coherence of Ionospheric Current Systems from Combined Ground Magnetometry and GPS Total Electron Content
metadata.description: We introduce a method for decomposing the spatial coherence of geomagnetic perturbations by altitude, combining SuperMAG ground magnetometer data with CODE Global Ionosphere Maps (GIM) of GPS total electron content (TEC). A two-layer Chapman model partitions TEC into solar EUV (F-region, 300 km) and auroral precipitation (E-region, 120 km) components, with the auroral fraction defined as a TEC-conserving column integral. Moran's I spatial autocorrelation statistic, computed on each modeled layer, yields three spatial-coherence measures (I_gnd, I_120, I_300) that carry largely independent information across eight geomagnetic events spanning 2000-2015 (combined R^2 = 0.12, 96 epochs). We stress that the two-layer split is a model, not a direct measurement of density at two altitudes. An altitude coherence switch, Delta = I_120 - I_300, oscillates by +/-0.4 during storms and tracks storm phase in the best-sampled sector; a per-sector decomposition shows its sign is sector-dependent, so we present it as a candidate diagnostic rather than a universal one. The same decomposition resolves magnetospheric spatial structure (the plasmapause boundary and the day-night asymmetry of the field-aligned current system) during magnetically quiet conditions (Kp ~ 1), demonstrating that the method does not depend on storm-amplitude perturbations to reveal magnetospheric organization. The method is robust to the choice of auroral fraction (f = 0.1-0.5), Chapman scale height (H = 40-80 km), and station network density (N >= 20). Independent cross-validation of a persistent Local Indicator of Spatial Association (LISA) anomaly near Kangerlussuaq, Greenland, using Swarm field-aligned currents, Van Allen Probes plasma composition, Swarm Langmuir probe density, and Swarm auroral oval boundaries confirms a magnetospheric origin at the Region 1 / Region 2 FAC boundary coincident with the plasmapause. The method provides a new diagnostic channel for ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling that is directly relevant to space weather nowcasting and geomagnetically induced current hazard assessment.
